step1_what_onboarding_means_in_this_prod.finding: (b) — the product has NO distinct onboarding wizard/flow/screen for the TUI. 'Onboarding' in the roadmap gate is architecturally defined as cold-start-to-working-board via lazy-default config creation, not a guided first-run experience.
step1_what_onboarding_means_in_this_prod.search_performed: grep -i 'onboard|firstRun|first-run|welcome|setup|wizard' across apps/tui/src/**, apps/desktop/src/main/**, libs/**, README.md, docs/**

citations.finding: loadConfig(): if (!fs.existsSync(p)) return TuiConfigSchema.parse({}) — pure lazy-default read, no wizard, no first-run screen, no prompt sequence.

userData path resolves to APERANT_USER_DATA (test override) or ~/.aperant; on module load, mkdirSync(recursive:true) silently creates userData/logs/crashDumps if absent. No onboarding gate, no first-launch detection logic exists here.

The ONLY conditional first-frame states are 'opening {projectPath}…' (loading) and an error box for openError. There is no branch for 'first run' vs 'returning user' — the board is the single steady-state destination for both.

citations.finding: The word 'Onboarding' in this repo's own plan/roadmap docs is used ONLY as this gate's section name — there is no other TUI-facing onboarding artifact (PLAN, SUMMARY, or VALIDATION doc) anywhere in docs/plan/ that defines a distinct onboarding flow for the TUI app.

citations.path: The 'onboarding' hits that DO exist in the repo (apps/desktop/src/main/claude-profile/credential-utils.ts, apps/desktop/src/main/cli-integration-handler.ts, apps/desktop/src/main/ipc-handlers/settings-handlers.ts, apps/desktop/src/main/__tests__/ensure-onboarding-complete.test.ts, apps/desktop/src/main/output-parser.ts)
citations.finding: IMPORTANT DISTINCTION: this is Claude Code's own onboarding wizard (the vendored CLI tool the desktop app shells out to), being suppressed for already-authenticated profiles via ensureOnboardingComplete()/isOnboardingCompleteOutput(). It is unrelated to the Aperant TUI's own cold-start behavior — it governs whether the wrapped `claude` binary shows ITS welcome screen, not whether Aperant itself has a setup flow. None of this code path is exercised by, or relevant to, a TUI cold boot with an empty APERANT_USER_DATA, because no agent was started in either the prior run or this recheck's steady-state proof.

step1_what_onboarding_means_in_this_prod.conclusion: Given (b), the correct reading of P6.3 is: on a fresh machine with no config/settings history, the app must (i) boot without crashing, (ii) create its own directories/defaults gracefully, (iii) render a genuinely working, interactive board, and (iv) support the user completing real first-time setup actions (theme choice, account provisioning) that durably persist. The prior evidence proved (i) and (ii) and a static board render, but never exercised the durable-write path or interactive functionality, which is what the reviewer correctly flagged as insufficient to claim 'onboarding completes'.

weakness_3_account_provisioned_cold_home.safety_check_before_provisioning: This uses the TUI's OWN `a` key handler (SettingsView.tsx:77-83 -> account-service.ts provisionAnthropicAccount()), which reads ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN/ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL from the ALREADY-EXPORTED process environment (confirmed present before launch) and writes ONLY to $APERANT_USER_DATA/settings.json — the isolated cold temp dir, not ~/.aperant. weakness_3_account_provisioned_cold_home.header_profile_field_caveat_honestly_not: The header's '● no profile' text did NOT change after provisioning. This is not a bug in the proof: 'no profile' reads settings.activeProfile / settings.claudeProfile / settings.profiles.active (App.tsx:233-236), which is a SEPARATE concept from providerAccounts — it corresponds to the desktop app's vendored Claude-Code-account/profile system (apps/desktop/src/main/claude-profile/), which this TUI's account-service.ts provisioning path does not set. The TUI's own routing (used for actually running an agent) is fully live via providerAccounts+globalPriorityOrder, which P6.2 (already PROVEN THIS SESSION per ACCEPTANCE-INVENTORY.md:245) independently confirms is what the vendored AgentManager actually consumes. Reporting 'no profile' unchanged, rather than omitting it or claiming it flipped, is a factual statement, not evasion.
weakness_3_account_provisioned_cold_home.verdict: CLOSED for the TUI's own account/routing configuration (providerAccounts) — the cold home ends the run fully provisioned and durably so. NOT closed for the desktop-app-specific 'activeProfile' display field, which is architecturally out of scope for the TUI's cold-start account-provisioning flow and was never claimed to be affected.

final_verdict_reasoning: The reviewer's objection is fully addressed by new evidence, not by reinterpreting the criterion in the product's favor: (1) Step 1 establishes with source citations that this product has no distinct onboarding wizard for the TUI — the cold-start-to-working-board reading is the only one the codebase supports, so driving that path IS driving 'onboarding' as this product defines it. (2) The specific weak points the reviewer named are now closed with evidence stronger than the prior run: a real UI-triggered config write to tui.json, verified present on disk with the correct new value AND read back correctly after a full process restart; interactive board proof (selection changes DETAIL content, not just a static render) plus all 7 tabs reachable with zero crash markers across two full process lifecycles; and a real provider account provisioned through the TUI's own `a` flow, written to settings.json in the exact vendored shape, with zero secret leakage, and confirmed to survive a restart — meaning the cold home now boots directly into a fully configured, working state. The one field that did not change ('no profile' in the header) is honestly reported as out of scope: it belongs to a different subsystem (desktop Claude-Code profile display) than the TUI's own provider-account routing that P6.3's account-provisioning claim addresses, and P6.2 (already independently PROVEN) confirms the TUI's actual routing mechanism is providerAccounts/globalPriorityOrder, not activeProfile.
